verdict.rationale: Both PRs fix the bug the same way: they rename CRM `customer_id` to `customerId` at load time and switch `invoiceRow` to `requireCustomer`. Behaviour is equivalent. A's tests are hermetic: they use a temp-dir fixture and check the error type as well as the message. B's new tests read the live `data/` directory, so they depend on the working directory and on monthly data that will change. B also committed without being asked, and its report has a confusing, garbled aside about checklist tools, while A's report flags the real risk of duplicate ids across systems.
a_issues: Import order puts ./customers.js before ./csv.js, which is not alphabetical
Report says the duplicate-id risk was not checked but gives no mitigation
b_issues: New sources tests depend on the real data/ files and the working directory, so they are brittle as the monthly data changes
Unknown-customer test only matches the message with a regex and does not check that the error is an UnknownReferenceError
Report has a garbled, irrelevant aside about 'crapper, dryer or mutator tools from  checklist' and a CRLF note
Does not mention the risk of the same customer id existing in both billing and CRM

verdict.rationale: Both changes fix the bug the same way: they map CRM `customer_id` to `customerId` at load time and route the export lookup through `requireCustomer`. That fixes INV-1041 and follows the README's data-error convention. B's tests are better. It uses an isolated temp-dir fixture with an exact `deepEqual` and checks that the error is an `UnknownReferenceError`. A's tests read the real `data/` directory and depend on the working directory. B's report is also cleaner and points out a real remaining risk (duplicate ids across systems), while A's report has confusing tool references and A committed without being asked.
a_issues: `tests/sources.test.js` reads the real `data/` directory, so the tests depend on production data and on the cwd.
The unknown-customer test matches only the message by regex and does not check the error type.
The report says the change was committed locally (43fa95a) although nobody asked for a commit.
The report mentions unclear 'crapper, dryer or mutator tools from checklist' and a CRLF→LF conversion warning, which adds noise and some doubt about line-ending churn.
b_issues: The `requireCustomer` import is placed before `csv.js`, breaking the existing alphabetical import order.
It does not check for, or guard against, duplicate customer ids across the two systems; this is acknowledged in the report but left unaddressed.
